chapter: Moving, Columbia Missouri and leaving home
title: Claude Hopkins and the heavy touch of Fats Waller
summary: Thompson was impressed by the soft, intellectual piano of Claude Hopkins, compared with the heavy touch of Fats Waller, whose happiness he doubts.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: And as I told you, I'd heard Fats Waller play, and several other musicians, incidentally. I remember hearing a pianist by the name of Claude Hopkins, in fact he was one of the first pianists that I heard that impressed me that he had a very intellectual and softer musical approach to playing jazz. I thought that he was --
Yes, yes, it was more finesseful.

As I said, Fats Waller was a comedian and he was a heavy man of statute, and a loud type of person although he was of good humor. But his touch was very heavy on the piano. That was the one thing that I noticed about Fats Waller playing, he was a very heavy. It was because, as I said, he was a large man, he was very happy -- at least he had the impression of being happy. I don't know -- I didn't know him that well to know whether he was happy or not. After reading the story of his life I doubt if he was very happy inside because he drank a lot of whiskey. But whiskey can sometimes make you think you're happy.
But this Claude Hawkins had a beautiful sound, he was recording from someplace in New York. It could have been the Cotton Club --
From the Roseland, I think he was broadcasting.
I'm not sure of the statistics.
